file.content: Benchmark contamination is widely assumed to inflate language model scores, yet the actual effect has never been systematically measured across model families. We perform controlled SFT injection at five dosage levels into five models spanning four independent families (7B--14.7B parameters) and discover that contamination produces not one effect but qualitatively different dose-response patterns---from immunity (mean $\Delta < 1$\,percentage point [pp] across three seeds) through monotonic benefit ($+$2.4pp mean) to catastrophic collapse ($-$9 to $-$25pp across seeds). Two patterns (Immune, Benefit) are attested in two or more independent families; Collapse and V-recovery are each observed in one family across all three seeds and require additional family-level replication. In our five-family sample, contamination vulnerability concentrates in the 65--70\% MMLU baseline band; models at extreme baselines show limited sensitivity. Counter-intuitively, the 14B Qwen model is 3$\times$ more fragile than 7B. These effects are benchmark-conditional: models harmed on MMLU can simultaneously benefit on GSM8K ($+$11pp), revealing asymmetric cross-benchmark transfer. Difference-in-differences analysis finds no item-specific memorization on MMLU (minimum detectable effect size 1.2--2.0pp); ARC has limited power (2.3--5.6pp). Profiles are robust: within-seed bootstrap stability exceeds 99.6\% for 4/5 MMLU families, though cross-seed sign consistency is 2/5. ARC-Challenge achieves 4/5 directional agreement despite its smaller item pool (1{,}172 vs.\ 14{,}042 items). We characterize contamination detection signal failure: Min-K\%++ exhibits directional reversal at small scales (paired Cohen's $d = -1.98$ at d100; $|d| > 1.4$ at d005), actively misleading practitioners. Simulation establishes that IRT-based contamination diagnosis requires ensemble sizes ($J \geq 50$) above current practice. Out-of-sample validation on a held-out fifth family (LLaMA-3.1-8B) confirms the profiles generalize: it is classified Immune despite a baseline matching OLMo-2's Benefit, showing that family-level factors beyond baseline ability---including pre-training data composition, tokenizer design, and training recipe---modulate vulnerability. Our findings demonstrate that ``contamination equals inflation'' is a gross oversimplification; model-specific dose-response profiling is necessary for reliable benchmark interpretation.
